candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0155.

options.A: Give the dose as ordered because ondansetron affects the QT interval only in clients who also have severe hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia.
options.B: Clarify the order because current labeling advises avoiding ondansetron in congenital long-QT syndrome due to QT prolongation and torsades risk.
options.C: Administer the medication with a beta blocker because rate control reliably eliminates the proarrhythmic effect of ondansetron in long-QT syndrome.
options.D: Give the dose and obtain an ECG only if syncope occurs because routine risk assessment before ondansetron is unnecessary in congenital long-QT syndrome.

candidate.rationale: Ondansetron labeling reports QT prolongation and postmarketing torsades de pointes and advises avoiding the drug in patients with congenital long-QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended for additional risk groups such as electrolyte abnormalities, heart failure, bradyarrhythmias, or other QT-prolonging drugs.
